examples.dm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no intention; Within those, there is not even an atom's worth of a station for consciousness. They do not dwell on any phenomena, but practice without a dwelling place; Without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no volition; Consciousness does not dwell in them even slightly. Not dwelling in all phenomena, they practice without dwelling, And without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतना च विज्ञान स्थानु अणुमात्र न भोन्ति तस्य । सो सर्वधर्म-अस्थितो अनिकेतचारी अपरीरिगृहीत लभते सुगतान बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: Those who engage in the practice of benefit and compassion, Having trained in this vidyā-mantra, the wise shall touch enlightenment; One should know that all forms of happiness, Whether conditioned or unconditioned, arise from this.
examples.gm: Those who practice the practices endowed with benefit and compassion, The wise ones, having trained in this mantra, will touch awakening. Whatever is conditioned happiness and unconditioned happiness, One should know that all those forms of happiness arise from this.
examples.sa: ये वा चरन्ति चरियां हितसानुकम्पाम् इह विद्यशिक्षित विदु स्पृशिष्यन्ति बोधिम् । ये सौख्य संस्कृत असंस्कृत ये च सौख्या सर्वे च सौख्य प्रसुता इतु वेदितव्याः ॥

examples.dm: However much the hosts of śrāvakas generate a mass of merit Through being endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, It cannot match even a fraction of a bodhisattva’s single thought of rejoicing; The mass of merit of the śrāvaka hosts cannot match even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Even if however many hosts of śrāvakas generate collections of merit, Fully endowed with generosity, ethical discipline, and meditation, Compared to a single mind of rejoicing of a bodhisattva, The heap of merit of the hosts of śrāvakas cannot match it.
examples.sa: यावन्ति श्रावकगणाः प्रसवन्ति पुण्यं दानं च शीलमपि भावनसंप्रयुक्तम् । स हि बोधिसत्त्व अनुमोदन एकचित्ते न च सर्वश्रावकगणे सिय पुण्यस्कन्धो ॥

examples.dm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no intention; Within those, there is not even an atom's worth of a station for consciousness. They do not dwell on any phenomena, but practice without a dwelling place; Without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: There is no form, no feeling, no perception, and no volition; Consciousness does not dwell in them even slightly. Not dwelling in all phenomena, they practice without dwelling, And without grasping, they attain the awakening of the Sugatas.
examples.sa: न च रुप वेदन न संज्ञ न चेतना च विज्ञान स्थानु अणुमात्र न भोन्ति तस्य । सो सर्वधर्म-अस्थितो अनिकेतचारी अपरीरिगृहीत लभते सुगतान बोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: For example, if the Lord of Nagas were not present in Lake Anavatapta, How could the rivers ever flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not grow, And the great ocean, too, would lack its many precious forms.
examples.gm: For example, if there were no nāga lord at Lake Anavatapta, How could rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not emerge, And the ocean would also not have many forms of jewels.
examples.sa: यथ नोपतप्त असतो भुजगाधिपस्य कुत नद्यप्रस्रवु भवेदिह जम्बुद्वीपे । असता नदीय फलपुष्प न संभवेयुः न च सागराण रतना भवि नैकरूपाः ॥

examples.dm: It is not for the sake of the increase, decrease, or grasping of form; Nor is it for the sake of grasping the various phenomena that one trains. While training, one also grasps omniscience itself; This very transcendence is the training of those who delight in excellence.
examples.gm: It is not for the sake of the increase, complete deterioration, or complete apprehension of form; Not training for the sake of completely apprehending various dharmas, Yet training and completely apprehending omniscience itself— Whatever definite emergence this is, this is the training that rejoices in qualities.
examples.sa: न च रुपवृद्धिपरिहाणिपरिग्रहाये न च शिक्षति विविधधर्मपरिग्रहाये । सर्वज्ञतां च परिगृह्णति शिक्षमाणो निर्यायती य इय शिक्ष गुणे रतानाम् ॥

examples.dm: Yet someone were to write down in a book this Mother of the Sugatas, From whom the Ten Powers of the Guides arise, And, bearing it, were to honor it with flowers and ointments, The merit of having worshiped stūpas would not approach even a fraction of that.
examples.gm: Whoever, regarding that from which the Guides of ten powers will arise, Writes this Mother of the Sugatas in a book, Retains it, and pays reverence with flowers and ointments, The merit of building stūpas and making offerings cannot match a fraction of that.
examples.sa: यश् चो इमां सुगतमात लिखित्व पुस्ते यत उत्पती दशबलान विनायकानाम् । धारेयि सत्करयि पुष्पविलेपनेहि कल पुण्य भोन्ति न स स्तूपि करित्व पूजाम् ॥

examples.dm: Yet a wise bodhisattva with skillful means Were to rejoice in the substance of those meritorious deeds, And fully dedicate it toward supreme, sublime enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings, By that complete dedication, one will outshine all living beings.
examples.gm: Whatever wise bodhisattva, skilled in means, Rejoices in their bases of meritorious actions, And fully dedicates them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings, By fully dedicating them, they outshine all beings.
examples.sa: यश् चो उपायकुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो तेषां स पुण्यक्रियवस्त्वनुमोदयित्वा । सत्त्वार्थ अग्रवरबोधयि नामयेया अभिभोति सर्वजगती परिणामयुक्तो ॥

examples.dm: From the time they first generate the aspiration for supreme enlightenment, Until the time the true Dharma of those guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors possess during that interval, Including the perfections and all the Buddha-qualities,
examples.gm: From when they first generated the mind for supreme awakening, Until the time the holy dharma of those Guides is exhausted, Whatever merit those Victors have during that time, And whatever is endowed with the perfections and whatever buddha-dharmas—
examples.sa: प्रथमं उपादु वरबोधयि चित्तुपादो यावत् सु धर्मक्षयकालु विनायकानाम् । एकस्मि तत्र चिय तेष जिनान पुण्यं सह युक्त पारमित येऽपि च बुद्धधर्माः ॥

examples.dm: Wisdom is the precursor to the practice of generosity, And likewise for ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration. It is the total sustainer that prevents virtuous qualities from being lost; This demonstrates the single nature of all phenomena.
examples.gm: Wisdom is what precedes giving; Ethical discipline, patience, joyous effort, and concentration are likewise. In order that virtuous dharmas are not wasted, it fully upholds them. This demonstrates all dharmas as having a single way.
examples.sa: पूर्वंगमा भवतु दानु ददन्तु प्रज्ञा शीले च क्षान्ति तथ वीर्य तथैव ध्याने । परिग्राहिका कुशलधर्म-अविप्रणाशे एका च सा अपि निदर्शयि सर्वधर्मान् ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are throughout Jambudvīpa without exception, If all of them were to generate the mind of supreme enlightenment, And were to practice generosity for many tens of millions of millennia, And were to dedicate it all as a cause for awakening for the sake of all beings,
examples.gm: However many sentient beings there are in Jambudvīpa without exception, If all of them, having generated the mind toward supreme awakening, Were to give gifts for many tens of millions of thousands of years, And dedicate it all as a cause for awakening for the benefit of beings;
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व निखिले इह जम्बुद्विपे ते सर्वि बोधिवरचित्त उपादयित्वा । दानं ददित्व बहुवर्षसहस्रकोटीः सर्वं च नामयि जगार्थनिदान बोधौ ॥

examples.dm: If someone were to diligently apply themselves to the supreme perfection of wisdom, And practice in accordance with it for even a single day, The mass of merit from that giving would not equal even a fraction of this. Therefore, one should always engage in wisdom without distraction.
examples.gm: Whoever visibly strives in the supreme perfection of wisdom, If they conform to it for even a single day, That aggregate of generosity cannot match a fraction of their merit; Therefore, one should always engage in wisdom without wavering.
examples.sa: यश् चैव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताभियुक्तो दिवसं पि अन्तमश एकनुवर्तयेया । कलपुण्य सो न भवती इह दानस्कन्धो तदतन्द्रितेन सद ओसरितव्य प्रज्ञा ॥

examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: It is taught that the way one grasps is the way one is completely afflicted; It is said that when "I" and "mine" are not observed, there is total purification. In this, without anything being defiled or purified, The Bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as there is apprehension, so is complete affliction taught; Not apprehending self and what belongs to self is taught as complete purification; In this, without anything becoming afflicted or completely pure, The bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ उद्ग्रहो तथ प्रकाशितु संकिलेशो व्योदान उक्त अहु मह्य अनोपलब्धि । न हि अत्र कश्चि यो क्लिश्यति शुध्यते वा प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वे ॥

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: For example, if the Lord of Nagas were not present in Lake Anavatapta, How could the rivers ever flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not grow, And the great ocean, too, would lack its many precious forms.
examples.gm: For example, if there were no nāga lord at Lake Anavatapta, How could rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not emerge, And the ocean would also not have many forms of jewels.
examples.sa: यथ नोपतप्त असतो भुजगाधिपस्य कुत नद्यप्रस्रवु भवेदिह जम्बुद्वीपे । असता नदीय फलपुष्प न संभवेयुः न च सागराण रतना भवि नैकरूपाः ॥

examples.dm: Whatever Buddhas of the past, numbering tens of millions of billions, Who reside in infinitely many billions of fields, and those who have passed into parinirvāṇa, Those protectors of the world, Teach the precious Dharma for the sake of completely ending suffering.
examples.gm: Whatever tens of millions of hundreds of billions of buddhas of the past, And whoever resides in many infinite thousands of tens of millions of fields, And whatever protectors of the world who have passed into nirvāṇa, Demonstrate the precious dharma in order to exhaust suffering:
examples.sa: ये बुद्धकोटिनियुता पुरिमा व्यतीता ये वा अनन्तबहुक्षेत्रसहस्रकोटयः । तिष्ठन्ति येऽपि परिनिर्वृत लोकनाथा देशन्ति धर्मरतनं दुखसंक्षयाय ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, if you wish to attain the supreme primordial wisdom of a Buddha, Have faith in this Mother of the Victors. For example, it would be unfitting to be like a merchant who, Having traveled to an island of jewels, returns home with his goods exhausted.
examples.gm: Therefore, if the supreme pristine wisdom of a buddha One wishes to touch, generate faith in this Mother of the Victors! For example, having gone to the island of jewels, a merchant Returning bereft of goods—it is not fitting to become like that.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु श्रद्दधत एव जिनान मातां यदि इच्छथा स्पृशितु उत्तमबुद्धज्ञानम् । सो वाणिजो यथ व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं मूलातु छेदन करित्व पुन आगमेया ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: Thus did the elder Subhūti request of the Protector of the World: "Please explain the signs of the ocean of qualities free from afflictions, And how those of great power do not turn back; O Victor, please grant a prophecy regarding even a mere portion of such qualities."
examples.gm: The elder Subhūti thoroughly requested the Protector of the World: "Ocean of Qualities, please teach the signs of those free from afflictions. How those of great power will not turn back again— Thus, may the Victor explain just a fraction of their qualities."
examples.sa: स्थविरो सुभूति परिपृच्छति लोकनाथं अरणाय लिङ्ग भणही गुणसागराणाम् । अविवर्तिया यथ भवन्ति महानुभावा तां व्याकुरुष्व जिनगुणान प्रदेशमात्रम् ॥

examples.dm: Dedicate generosity, ethical discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Meditative concentration, and wisdom toward awakening. Do not harbor a superior conceit by clinging to the aggregates of awakening; Thus should it be taught to those who are beginners.
examples.gm: "Completely dedicate generosity, discipline, patience, as well as diligence, Concentration, and wisdom to enlightenment. Do not hold supreme views by being attached to enlightenment or the aggregates"— They should instruct beginners in that way.
examples.sa: दानं च शीलमपि क्षान्ति तथैव वीर्यं ध्यानानि प्रज्ञ परिणामयितव्य बोधौ । न च बोधिस्कन्ध विमृशित्व परामृशेया ये आदिकर्मिक न देशयितव्य एवम् ॥

examples.dm: Both are distant and will become like flesh-eating demons; Both will cause their own commitments to degenerate. How can there be awakening for those who are hostile and devoid of patience? At that time, the Māras and their factions will be delighted.
examples.gm: "Those two will become distant, and they will become like flesh-eating demons; Both will cause their own promises to degenerate. How can there be awakening for those who are hostile and devoid of patience?" At that time, the Māras along with their factions will become joyful.
examples.sa: उभि एति दूरि भविष्यन्ति पिशाचतुल्या उभि एति आत्म करिष्यन्ति प्रतिज्ञहानिम् । दुष्टान क्षान्तिविकलान कुतोऽस्ति बोधि तद मारु तुष्टु भवती नमुचीसपक्षो ॥

examples.dm: The body of one who abides in patience becomes completely pure, Possessing the thirty-two major marks and infinite power; They proclaim the supreme Dharma of emptiness to sentient beings. Wise and patient, they bring joy to the world.
examples.gm: The body of one who abides in patience becomes completely pure; With the thirty-two marks and boundless power and strength, They proclaim the supreme empty dharma to sentient beings; Beings will rejoice in this wise one endowed with patience.
examples.sa: क्षान्तीस्थितस्य परिशुध्यति आत्मभावो द्वात्रिंशलक्षणप्रभाव अनन्तपारो । सत्त्वान शून्यवरधर्म निशामयाती प्रियु भोति सर्वजगती क्षममाणु विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: The teaching of the Dharma, the listening, and whatever is taught, The attainment of the result, the Pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the clarity of the wise— The Tathāgata has taught that all these are like an illusion.
examples.gm: The one who teaches the Dharma, the one who listens, and whatever is to be taught, The attainment of the fruit, the pratyekabuddhas, and likewise the Protectors of the World, And whatever nirvāṇa is attained by the brilliant wise ones— All these are taught by the Tathāgata to be like an illusion.
examples.sa: यो धर्म भाष्यति य भाष्यति भाष्यमाणां फलप्राप्त प्रत्ययजिनो तथ लोकनाथो । निर्वाणतो अधिगतो विदुपण्डितेहि सर्वे त आत्मज निदृष्ट तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: Whoever, as a protector, practices this perfection of wisdom, And whoever holds and masters it with devotion, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water; Mara and the factions of Mara will find no opportunity to harm them.
examples.gm: The perfection of wisdom, in which the Protectors practice— Whoever respects, apprehends, and masters it, Will not be harmed by poison, weapons, fire, or water, And Māra and the factions of Māra will find no opportunity against them.
examples.sa: य इमां ग्रहीष्यति पर्यापुणती स नित्यं प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति नाथाः । विष वह्नि शस्त्र उदकं न क्रमाति तस्यो ओतारु मारु न च विन्दति मारपक्षो ॥

examples.dm: This Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra of knowledge; It pacifies the misery and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Those protectors of the worlds in the ten directions, past and present, Who train in this mantra of knowledge will become unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.gm: This perfection of wisdom of the Victors is a great mantra; It pacifies the dharmas of sorrow and suffering of the many realms of sentient beings. Whichever Protectors of the World are in the past, and whichever are in the ten directions, Having trained in this mantra, became unsurpassed kings of physicians.
examples.sa: महविद्य प्रज्ञ अयु पारमिता जनानां दुखधर्मशोकशमनी पृथुसत्त्वधातोः । येऽतीत येऽपि च दशद्दिश लोकनाथा इम विद्य शिक्षित अनुत्तरवैद्यराजाः ॥

examples.dm: Whoever practices here does not conceptualize the Buddha-qualities, Nor do they conceptualize the powers, the bases of miraculous power, awakening, or peace. They practice through the blessing of non-conceptuality, free from mental construction; This is the practice of the supreme Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: Whoever practices here does not conceptualize the qualities of a Buddha; They do not conceptualize the powers, the bases of miraculous power, or peaceful enlightenment; Non-conceptualizing and free from concepts, they practice through blessing; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: चरमाणु यो न इह कल्पयि बुद्धधर्मां बल ऋद्धिपाद न च कल्पयि बोधि शान्ताम् । अविकल्पकल्पविगतोऽधिष्ठानचारी एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: So too, the bodhisattva who has gone to the jewel island of emptiness, Having attained the meditative concentrations, faculties, and powers, Does not take delight in merely touching nirvana alone, And does not leave the suffering of sentient beings behind.
examples.gm: Likewise, a bodhisattva who has gone to the jewel island of emptiness, And attained the powers of the faculties of concentration, Does not merely delight in touching nirvāṇa, And leave sentient beings in suffering.
examples.sa: एमेव शून्यत व्रजित्वन रत्नद्वीपं लब्ध्वान ध्यान बल इन्द्रिय बोधिसत्त्वो । किंचापि निर्वृति स्पृशेदभिनन्दमानो अपि सर्वसत्त्व दुखिता मनसी भवन्ति ॥

examples.dm: A bodhisattva who strives for the benefit of beings and has attained meditative concentration, Powers, faculties, liberations, and absorptions—if one treats them with contempt, Thinking, "This person does not practice in forest isolation," The Victor has declared that such a person dwells within the domain of Māra.
examples.gm: When a bodhisattva striving for the benefit of beings attains dhyāna, Powers, faculties, liberations, and samādhi, If one despises them, thinking, "This is not the conduct of isolated monasteries," The Victorious One says they abide in the domain of Māra.
examples.sa: सो चंक्रमार्थम् अभियुक्तकबोधिसत्त्वान् बलध्यान-इन्द्रियविमोक्षसमाधिप्राप्तान् । अभिमन्यते न इमि रण्यविवेकचारी न विवेकगोचरु अयं हि जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: For the sake of other beings and persons, the bodhisattva of pure intention Applies themselves with diligent exertion to the perfection of perseverance. For example, just as a female slave carrying water is powerless and under the control of her master, So too do the heroic beings proceed under the control of all sentient beings.
examples.gm: For the sake of other sentient beings and persons, the perfectly pure bodhisattva Manifestly exerts themselves and acts in the perfection of diligence; For example, a servant woman drawing water has no power of her own, but is under the power of her master; Similarly, the heroes act under the power of all sentient beings.
examples.sa: परसत्त्वपुद्गलनिदान विशुद्धसत्त्वा विचरन्ति वीर्यबलपारमिताभियुक्ताः । यथ कुम्भदासि अवशावश भर्तिकस्य तथ सर्वसत्त्ववशतामुपयान्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who wishes to remain for a long time in cyclic existence, A yogi who perseveres in the welfare of sentient beings and the purification of the realm, If they do not give rise to even a speck of weariness, They possess the perfection of diligence and are never negligent.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva wishes to cycle in saṃsāra for a long time, A yogi exerting themselves for the benefit of sentient beings and purifying the realms, If they do not generate even an atom of a weary mind, They are endowed with the perfection of diligence and are free from idleness.
examples.sa: यो बोधिसत्त्व चिरसंसरणाभिप्रायो सत्त्वार्थ क्षेत्रपरिशोधनयुक्तयोगी । न च खेदबुद्धि अणुमात्र उपादियाति सो वीर्यपारमितयुक्त अतन्द्रितश् च ॥

examples.dm: If unskilled bodhisattvas count out tens of millions of eons, And, perceiving it as a long time, strive for enlightenment with a sense of hardship, They will suffer for a long duration while practicing the authentic Dharma. Such individuals are lazy, and their perfection of diligence declines.
examples.gm: The unwise bodhisattva counts tens of millions of eons; If they perceive them as long, they suffer in accomplishing awakening; When accomplishing the authentic dharma, they suffer for a long time; Their perfection of diligence diminishes and they possess laziness.
examples.sa: सचि कल्पकोटि गणये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो चिरसंज्ञ बोधि समुदानिय तेन दुःखे । चिरदुःख भेष्यति समाचरमाणु धर्मं ततु वीर्यपारमितहीन कुसीदरूपो ॥

examples.dm: When wise and learned bodhisattvas, contemplating non-arising, Practice in this way, Though they generate great compassion, they have no perception of sentient beings; This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Whenever a wise, understanding bodhisattva Reflects on non-arising and practices in this way, Generating great compassion without the perception of sentient beings, This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यस्मिंश् च कालि समये विदु बोधिसत्त्वो एवं चरन्तु अनुपादु विचिन्तयित्वा । महतीं जनेति करुणां न च सत्त्वसंज्ञा एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: Yogis who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom, Though they generate great compassion, have no perception of sentient beings. At that time, those wise ones become the objects of offering for all the world; They always make meaningful use of the alms of the country.
examples.gm: The yogi practicing the supreme perfection of wisdom, Even when generating great compassion, has no perception of sentient beings; At that time, the wise one becomes a field of generosity for all beings, And always meaningfully fully enjoys the alms of the realm.
examples.sa: चरमाणु प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय योगी महतीं जनेति करुणां न च सत्त्वसंज्ञा । तद भोन्ति सर्वजगती विदु दक्षिणीया सततं अमोघु परिभुञ्जति राष्ट्रपिण्डम् ॥

examples.dm: Suppose someone were to make offerings to the stūpas Of the Sugatas who have passed into parinirvāṇa, constructing them of the seven precious gems, And were to fill a thousand million buddha-fields With as many stūpas of the Sugatas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges;
examples.gm: If someone, of the completely parinirvāṇized Sugata, Were to build stūpas from the seven precious things and make offerings, and with those stūpas of the Sugata, as numerous as the Ganges' Sands, were to fill thousands of millions of fields;
examples.sa: परिनिर्वृतस्य सुगतस्य करेय्य स्तूपां पूजेय सप्तरतनामयु कश्चिद् एव । तेहि प्रपूर्ण सिय क्षेत्रसहस्रकोट्यो यथ गङ्गवालिकसमैः सुगतस्य स्तूपैः ॥

examples.dm: However many sentient beings there are—the lesser, the middling, and the superior— The Sugata taught that they all arise from ignorance. When conditions assemble, the machine of suffering fully emerges; That machine of ignorance neither exhausts nor increases.
examples.gm: However many inferior, middling, and supreme sentient beings there are, The Sugatas have taught that they all arise from ignorance; When conditions come together, the machine of suffering perfectly arises, Yet that machine of ignorance has no exhaustion and no increase.
examples.sa: यावन्त सत्त्व मृदुमध्यमुत्कृष्ट लोके सर्वे अविद्यप्रभवा सुगतेन उक्ताः । सामग्रिप्रत्ययु प्रवर्तति दुःखयन्त्रो न च यन्त्र क्षीयति अविद्य न चापि वृद्धिः ॥

examples.dm: Therefore, one should train in dedication in this way: Whatever the nature, the source, and the characteristics of that virtue Are as known by those Victors, One should rejoice in it and dedicate it in exactly that same way.
examples.gm: Therefore, one should train in dedicating in this way: Just as those Victors know that virtue— Whatever its aspect, whatever its origin, whatever its defining characteristic— Rejoicing in it, one perfectly dedicates it in exactly that way.
examples.sa: तस्मा हु नामपरिणामन शिक्षितव्या यथ ते जिना कुशल एव प्रजानयन्ति । यज्जातियोऽयं प्रभवो यदलक्षणं च अनुमोदमी तथ तथा परिणामयामि ॥

examples.dm: Just as the perfection of wisdom is empty of intrinsic characteristics, One should understand that all these phenomena are likewise empty of such characteristics. When one thoroughly understands that all phenomena are empty and signless, To practice in such a manner is to practice the wisdom of the Sugatas.
examples.gm: Just as the perfection of wisdom is empty of characteristics, Knowing all these phenomena to be similar to that characteristic, If one thoroughly knows phenomena as empty and signless, Practicing like that is the wisdom practice of the Sugata.
examples.sa: यथ प्रज्ञपारमित शून्यत लक्षणेन तथलक्षणा य इमि जानति सर्वधर्मान् । शून्यानलक्षण प्रजानयमान धर्मान् एवं चरन्तु चरती सुगतान प्रज्ञाम् ॥

examples.dm: Those who practice in that way are the moons of speakers who live an excellent life; They are the refuge, the protector, and the dwelling place of beings. They are the support, the intellect, the island, and the guide for those seeking benefit, The illuminator, the lamp, the unshakeable speaker of the supreme Dharma.
examples.gm: Practicing thus, those oceans of goodness, moons of speech, Are the refuge, the defender, and the resting place of beings; They are the support, the mind, the island, and the supreme guides seeking their welfare; They are illuminating lamps, speakers of the supreme dharma, and are unperturbed.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्त गुणसागर वादिचन्द्राः त्राणा भवन्ति जगती शरणा च लेना । गति बुद्धि द्वीप परिणायक अर्थकामाः प्रद्योत उल्क वरधर्मकथी अक्षोभ्याः ॥

examples.dm: Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five objects of sensory desire, If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And maintain the mental orientation toward omniscience, thinking, "I must achieve buddhahood," The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
examples.gm: Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the five sensory pleasures, If they have taken refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and the noble Sangha, And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish buddhahood!" The wise one should be known as abiding in the perfection of discipline.
examples.sa: यदि पञ्च कामगुण भुञ्जति बोधिसत्त्वो बुद्धं च धर्म शरणागतु आर्यसंघम् । सर्वज्ञता च मनसी भविष्यामि बुद्धो स्थितु शीलपारमित वेदयितव्य विज्ञो ॥

examples.dm: In this way, those who practice the supreme perfection of wisdom, Acting through wisdom, skillful means, strength, and miraculous powers, As long as their roots of virtue are not yet complete, So long will they not attain that supreme emptiness.
examples.gm: Likewise, engaging in the supreme perfection of wisdom, Thoroughly practicing by means of the power of wisdom, skillful means, and miracles, As long as their roots of virtue are not perfected, For that long they do not attain that supreme emptiness.
examples.sa: एमेव प्रज्ञवरपारमितां चरन्तो प्रज्ञा उपाय बल ऋद्धि विचारमाणो । तावन् न तां परमशून्यत प्रापुणोति यावन् न ते कुशलमूल भवन्ति पूर्णाः ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva, having given a gift to living beings, Does not regard it as their own and has no attachment to the object, From that, the roots of virtue will grow to have great power, Like the bright orb of the waxing moon in a cloudless sky.
examples.gm: If the bodhisattva, having given gifts to beings, Does not make them "mine" and is unsparing of entities, Their roots of virtue will increase with great power, Like the radiant, cloudless moon disk in the waxing fortnight.
examples.sa: यदि बोधिसत्त्व ददमान जगस्य दानं ममतां न तत्र करयेन् न च वस्तुप्रेम । ततु वर्धते कुशलमूल महानुभावो चन्द्रो व तत्र प्रभमण्डलु शुक्लपक्षे ॥

examples.dm: Those who have entered into the supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoice from the depths of their hearts in the generation of the mind of enlightenment; Though one might find the measure of the three thousandfold world system and Mount Meru by weighing them on a scale, The virtue of such rejoicing is not like that.
examples.gm: Regarding those who have fully entered supreme, irreversible awakening, Rejoicing from the depths of one's heart in their generation of the mind— The Mount Meru of a trichiliocosm could be measured by weighing it on a scale, But the virtue of that rejoicing is not like that.
examples.sa: अविवर्तियस्य वरबोधयि प्रस्थितस्य यो चित्तुपादु अनुमोदितु आशयेन । त्रिसहस्र मेरु तुलयित्व सियाप्रमाणो न त्वेव तस्य कुशलस्यनुमोदनाये ॥

examples.dm: Any bodhisattva who possesses the excellent quality of patience— Suppose someone were to fill the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offer them to the Knower of the World, To the Buddhas, Arhats, and Pratyekabuddhas; The mass of merit from that giving would not equal even a fraction of this.
examples.gm: Whatever bodhisattva is endowed with the excellent dharma of patience, Compared to someone who fills the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offers them to the Knowers of the World, The Buddhas, arhats, and solitary realizers, That mass of generosity cannot match a fraction of the merit of the former.
examples.sa: सो बोधिसत्त्व क्षमते गुणधर्मयुक्तो यश् चैव रत्नभरितं त्रिसहस्र दद्यात् । बुद्धान लोकविदुनार्हतप्रत्ययानां कलपुण्य सो न भवते इह दानस्कन्धे ॥

examples.dm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victors thinks, "These sentient beings are ethical, but those are unethical," Engaging in such diverse perceptions, they are utterly lacking in ethical discipline; Their morality has degenerated, and they lack completely purified morality.
examples.gm: If a bodhisattva practicing the path of the Victorious Ones Thinks, "These sentient beings have discipline; these have broken discipline," By engaging in such diverse perceptions, their discipline is completely broken; Their discipline degenerates, and they lack completely pure discipline.
examples.sa: यदि बोधिसत्त्व चरमाणु जिनान मार्गे इमि शीलवानिमि दुशील करोति सत्त्वान् । नानात्वसंज्ञप्रसृतो परमं दुशीलो अपि छिद्रशीलु न तु सो परिशुद्धशीलो ॥

examples.dm: Any pure being who possesses such morality as this, Is without bias toward anything pleasant or unpleasant. They give away their heads, hands, and feet without a trace of discouragement; They give away all their possessions, remaining forever free from attachment.
examples.gm: Any pure sentient being who thus possesses discipline Has no view of anything as pleasant or unpleasant. Giving away their head, hands, and feet, they have no shrinking mind; Giving away all their possessions, they are always free from clinging.
examples.sa: यो एवशीलसमन्वागतु निष्प्रपञ्चो अनपेक्षको भवति सर्वप्रियाप्रियेषु । शिरहस्तपाद त्यजमान अदीनचित्तो सर्वास्तित्यागि भवते सततं अलीनो ॥

examples.dm: Establishing the highest joy, respect, and faith, Having cleared away the obscurations of the afflictions and transcended all stains, Listen to this perfection of wisdom of the noble ones, who are dedicated to the welfare of beings, And to that which is the conduct of the heroic ones.
examples.gm: Having established supreme joy, respect, and faith, Having removed obscurations and afflictions and passed beyond stains, The perfection of wisdom of the gentle ones engaged in the benefit of beings, Listen to that in which the heroes practice.
examples.sa: पर प्रेम गौरव प्रसाद उपस्थपित्वा प्रजहित्व आवरण क्लेशमलातिक्रान्ताः । शृणुता जगार्थमभिप्रस्थित सुरव्रतानां प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति शूराः ॥

examples.dm: If one asks, "Why is this one called a 'great being' (mahāsattva)?" Because they have become the foremost among the vast assembly of sentient beings, And because they sever the great thicket of views within the realm of sentient beings; For that reason, they are truly called a "great being."
examples.gm: Why are they called a "great being"? Because they become the supreme among great multitudes of sentient beings, and sever the great views of the realms of sentient beings; Therefore, they are proclaimed to be a "great being."
examples.sa: महसत्त्व सोऽथ केनोच्यति कारणेन महताय अत्र अयु भेष्यति सत्त्वराशेः । दृष्टीगतां महति छिन्दति सत्त्वधातोः महसत्त्व तेन हि प्रवुच्यति कारणेन ॥

examples.dm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, pleasant and unpleasant, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness; One does not dwell in the attainment of the fruit or the stage of an arhat, Nor does one dwell in the stage of a pratyekabuddha or likewise the stage of a buddha.
examples.gm: Permanent and impermanent, happiness and suffering, attractive and unattractive, Self and selflessness, suchness and likewise emptiness, Attaining the fruit, and not abiding in the level of an arhat, Not abiding in the level of a pratyekabuddha, and likewise not in the level of a buddha.
examples.sa: नित्यम् अनित्यसुखदुःखशुभाशुभं ति आत्मन्य् अनात्मि तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् । फलप्राप्तिताय अथितो अरहन्तभूमौ प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ ॥

examples.dm: Even if the Teacher were to remain for as many eons As there are grains of sand in the Ganges and proclaim the word "sentient being," Since they are pure from the beginning, how could a sentient being ever be born? This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Even if the Teacher were to remain for as many Aeons as there are grains of sand, and proclaim the word "sentient being," Since they are pure from the very beginning, how could a sentient being arise? This is the practice of the supreme perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: सचि गङ्गवालुकसमानि स्थिहित्व कल्पां सत्त्वेति शब्द परिकीर्तयि नायकोऽयम् । सत्त्वस्य्’ उपादु कुतु भेष्यति आदिशुद्धो एषा स प्रज्ञवरपारमिताय चर्या ॥

examples.dm: The Victor, having been asked a question by Śakra, replied: If there were Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would still take this very Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The Victor fully asked Śakra a question, and he replied: "Even if there were buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, And all of them were filled to the brim with the relics of the Victors, I would take this very perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: शक्रो जिनेन परिपृच्छितु प्रश्नमाहु सचि गङ्गवालिकसमा सिय बुद्धक्षेत्राः । जिनधातु सर्वि परिपूरित चूडिबद्धा इमम् एव प्रज्ञवरपारमिताहु गृह्णे ॥

examples.dm: For example, if the Lord of Nagas were not present in Lake Anavatapta, How could the rivers ever flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not grow, And the great ocean, too, would lack its many precious forms.
examples.gm: For example, if there were no nāga lord at Lake Anavatapta, How could rivers flow here in Jambudvīpa? If there were no rivers, flowers and fruits would not emerge, And the ocean would also not have many forms of jewels.
examples.sa: यथ नोपतप्त असतो भुजगाधिपस्य कुत नद्यप्रस्रवु भवेदिह जम्बुद्वीपे । असता नदीय फलपुष्प न संभवेयुः न च सागराण रतना भवि नैकरूपाः ॥

examples.dm: If one conceives of it in terms of signs, that is not a dedication. If there are no signs, that is the dedication to enlightenment. Just as eating fine food that has been mixed with poison, The Victor has taught that focusing on virtuous qualities is the same.
examples.gm: If one acts upon signs, that is not dedication; But if there are no signs, it is dedication to awakening. Just like eating excellent food mixed with poison, The Victor has declared that apprehending white dharmas is like that.
examples.sa: सचि सो निमित्त कुरुते न च मानयाति अथ आनिमित्त परिणामित भोन्ति बोधौ । विषसृष्ट भोजनु यथैव क्रियाप्रणीतो तथ शुक्लधर्मौपलम्भ जिनेन उक्तो ॥

examples.dm: The third chapter teaches the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, the heroic practitioners Truly transcend the three realms, yet they do not enter a narrow liberation. Although they have eliminated the afflictions, they manifest birth; Although they are free from aging, sickness, and death, they manifest passing away.
examples.gm: The third chapter: teaching the knowledge of all bases. Through the perfection of wisdom, wherever the hero practices, They completely transcend the three realms, yet are not liberated; Though afflictions are cleared away, they display birth; Though without aging, sickness, and death, they display death and transmigration.
examples.sa: त्रैधातुकं समतिक्रान्त न बोधिसत्त्वा क्लेशापनीत उपपत्ति निदर्शयन्ति । जरव्याधिमृत्युविगताश् च्युति दर्शयन्ति प्रज्ञाय पारमित यत्र चरन्ति धीराः ॥

examples.dm: When writing down this Perfection of Wisdom of the Victors, Various and diverse kinds of flashes of inspiration will arise; Yet if, without having benefited sentient beings, they vanish as swiftly as lightning, This complete deterioration is the work of Māra.
examples.gm: When copying this perfection of wisdom of the Victors, Various differing modes of confidence will arise; Yet without accomplishing the benefit of beings, swiftly like lightning, They will completely fade away; this is the work of Māra.
examples.sa: प्रतिभान नेक विविधानि उपपद्यिष्यन्ति लिखमान प्रज्ञ इमु पारमिता जिनानाम् । युत शीघ्र विद्युत यथा परिहायिष्यन्ति अकरित्व अर्थ जगती इमु मारकर्म ॥

examples.dm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the Arhats, The suchness of the Pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the Bodhisattvas— These are a single suchness, devoid of entities, a non-dual suchness; The Tathāgata knows this Perfection of Wisdom.
examples.gm: The suchness of the world and the suchness of the arhats, The suchness of the pratyekabuddhas and the suchness of the sons of the Victors: Are oneness, devoid of entities, not other; they are suchness; The perfection of wisdom is known by the Tathāgata.
examples.sa: लोकस्य या तथत या तथतार्हतानां । प्रत्येकबुद्धतथता तथता जिनानाम् । एकैव भावविगता तथता अनन्या प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुद्ध तथागतेन ॥

examples.dm: Whoever sees in that way sees all phenomena. Just as a king remains impartial while his ministers perform all the tasks, Whatever activities of the Buddhas and teachings of the Śrāvakas there may be, The Perfection of Wisdom performs them all.
examples.gm: Whoever sees in that way sees all dharmas. Just as a king sits in equanimity while his ministers do everything, Whatever deeds of the Buddhas and dharmas of the śrāvakas there are, All of them are done by the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यो एव पश्यति स पश्यति सर्वधर्मान् सर्वान् अमात्यकिरिया ति उपेक्ष्य राजा । यावन्ति बुद्धक्रिय धर्मत श्रावकाणां प्रज्ञाय पारमित सर्व करोति तानि ॥

examples.dm: Those who practice in that way are the moons of speakers who live an excellent life; They are the refuge, the protector, and the dwelling place of beings. They are the support, the intellect, the island, and the guide for those seeking benefit, The illuminator, the lamp, the unshakeable speaker of the supreme Dharma.
examples.gm: Practicing thus, those oceans of goodness, moons of speech, Are the refuge, the defender, and the resting place of beings; They are the support, the mind, the island, and the supreme guides seeking their welfare; They are illuminating lamps, speakers of the supreme dharma, and are unperturbed.
examples.sa: एवं चरन्त गुणसागर वादिचन्द्राः त्राणा भवन्ति जगती शरणा च लेना । गति बुद्धि द्वीप परिणायक अर्थकामाः प्रद्योत उल्क वरधर्मकथी अक्षोभ्याः ॥

examples.dm: Whoever wishes to set forth in this Buddha vehicle Should train with an even mind toward all beings, the recognition of them as parents, A helpful attitude, and a loving heart, Being without harshness, remaining straightforward, and speaking gentle words.
examples.gm: Whoever desires to definitely emerge in this vehicle of the Buddha, With an even mind toward all beings, perceiving them as parents, Should act with an attitude of benefit and a mind of loving-kindness, Be free from rigidity, straightforward, and speak gentle words.
examples.sa: निर्यायनाय य इच्छति बुद्धज्ञाने समचित्त सर्वजगती पितृमातृसंज्ञा । हितचित्त मैत्रमन एव पराक्रमेय्या अखिलार्जवो मृदुगिराय पराक्रमेय्या ॥

examples.dm: They have completely avoided the borderlands and the regions of barbarian peoples. They are never uncertain about their own stage, remaining as steadfast as Mount Meru. They would even sacrifice their lives for the sake of the Dharma and are devoted to the diligence of yoga. One should know that these are the signs of the state of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: They completely abandon the borderlands of uncivilized border-dwellers. Without self-doubt, they are always like Mount Sumeru. Giving up even their lives for the sake of the dharma, they vividly strive in yoga. One should know that these are the signs of an irreversible one.
examples.sa: प्रत्यन्तम्लेच्छजनवर्जित-अन्तदेशाः स्वकभूमि काङ्क्षविगताः सद मेरुकल्पाः । धर्मार्थ जीवित त्यजन्ति प्रयुक्तयोगा अविवर्तियान इमि लिङ्ग प्रजानितव्या ॥

examples.dm: The fifth chapter explains the clear realization of the pinnacle. One who does not desire the level of an Arhat, the wisdom of a Pratyekabuddha, Or the three realms, even in a dream, But sees the Buddhas and teaches the Dharma to beings— One should understand that this is the prophecy of non-retrogression.
examples.gm: Chapter Five: Teaching the Clear Realization of the Peak. The stage of an arhat and the pristine wisdom of a pratyekabuddha, And the three realms, they do not desire even in dreams; Seeing the buddhas and teaching the dharma to wanderers, They should be known as irreversible and prophesied.
examples.sa: अर्हन्तभूमिम् अपि प्रत्ययबुद्धभूमौ त्रैधातुकं न स्पृशते सुपिनान्तरेऽपि । बुद्धांश् च पश्यति कथेति जनस्य धर्मं अविवर्तियेति अयु व्याकृतु वेदितव्यो ॥

examples.dm: Whether one dwells in a town or in a forest, If one is free from the mind of the two vehicles and is certain of supreme enlightenment, This is the solitude of those who have entered into the service of beings; Any bodhisattva who feels superior to them has degraded themselves.
examples.gm: Whether abiding in a village or else in an isolated monastery, If free from the minds of the two vehicles and certain of supreme awakening, This is the solitude of those engaged in the benefit of beings; That conceited bodhisattva ruins themselves.
examples.sa: ग्रामान्ति यो विहरते अथवा अरण्ये द्वययानचित्तविगतो नियतोऽग्रबोधिम् । एषो विवेकु जगदर्थभिप्रस्थितानां आत्मा क्षिणोति तुलयेय स बोधिसत्त्वो ॥

examples.dm: It is taught that the way one grasps is the way one is completely afflicted; It is said that when "I" and "mine" are not observed, there is total purification. In this, without anything being defiled or purified, The Bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.gm: Just as there is apprehension, so is complete affliction taught; Not apprehending self and what belongs to self is taught as complete purification; In this, without anything becoming afflicted or completely pure, The bodhisattva realizes the perfection of wisdom.
examples.sa: यथ उद्ग्रहो तथ प्रकाशितु संकिलेशो व्योदान उक्त अहु मह्य अनोपलब्धि । न हि अत्र कश्चि यो क्लिश्यति शुध्यते वा प्रज्ञाय पारमित बुध्यति बोधिसत्त्वे ॥

examples.dm: However, when those wise ones possess intense resolve, And day and night look toward the supreme meaning of the perfection of wisdom, At that time, their body, mind, and speech move like a bird in the sky; How could the factions of darkness ever find an opportunity against them?
examples.gm: When those wise ones, possessing intense resolve, Behold the supreme meaning of the perfection of wisdom day and night, At that time, their body, mind, and speech move like a bird in the sky; How could the associates of the dark one find an opportunity?
examples.sa: यथ ते भवन्ति विदु आशयसंप्रयुक्ता दिवरात्रि प्रज्ञवरपारमितार्थदर्शी । तद कायचित्त खगपक्षिसतुल्यभूता अवतारु सो कुतु लभिष्यति कृष्णबन्धुः ॥

examples.dm: In this way, the wise light-makers train in wisdom; They do not give rise to even a single unvirtuous thought. Just as darkness cannot remain in the space before it When it is overwhelmed by the rays of the sun moving through the sky,
examples.gm: The wise light-makers train in wisdom like that; They do not generate even a single non-virtuous mind. Just as, when outshone by the rays of the sun moving in the sky, Darkness does not remain in the space before it.
examples.sa: शिक्षन्तु एव विदु प्रज्ञ प्रभंकराणां नोत्पद्यते अकुशलमपि एकचित्तम् । सूर्ये यथा गगनि गच्छति अन्तरीक्षे रश्मीगते न स्थिहते पुरतोऽन्धकारम् ॥

examples.dm: In the midst of a crowd, a conjured person does not think, "I must please these people," and yet they perform that very action; Although they are seen displaying various miraculous feats, They possess no body, no mind, and not even a name.
examples.gm: In the midst of people, an illusory person does not think, "I will please these people," yet still pleases them; Though seen to display various miracles, They have no body, no mind, and not even a name.
examples.sa: यथ मायकारपुरुषस्य न एव भोति ते शिष्य मां जनत सो च करोति कार्यम् । पश्यन्ति तं विविध कार्यु निदर्शयन्तं न च तस्य कायु न पि चित्त न नामधेयम् ॥

examples.dm: Though birds dwell in the sky, they do not fall; Though fish dwell in the water, they do not suffocate or die. Likewise, through the power of meditative concentration, Bodhisattvas Who have reached the far shore dwell in emptiness but do not pass into nirvāṇa.
examples.gm: A bird dwells in the sky, yet does not fall; A fish dwells in water, yet does not suffocate and die; Likewise, the bodhisattva, by the powers of concentration, Having reached the other shore, dwells in emptiness and does not pass into nirvāṇa.
examples.sa: आकाशि पक्षि विहराति न चो पताति दकमध्यि मत्स्य विहराति न चो मराति । एमेव ध्यानबलपारगु बोधिसत्त्वो शून्याविहारि न च निर्वृति प्रापुणाति ॥

examples.dm: This is a marvelous and wondrous accumulation of qualities: Abiding in meditative concentration and stabilization, they are without signs. If those who abide therein should have their bodies perish, They will be reborn in the desire realm exactly according to their intentions.
examples.gm: This is the marvelous wonder of accumulating qualities: Having abided in the samādhis of the dhyānas, they have no signs; If the bodies of those who abide in them were to fall apart, They are again born in the desire realm according to their intention.
examples.sa: आश्चर्यम् अद्भुतम् इदं गुणसंचयानां ध्याने समाधि विहरन्ति निमित्त नास्ति । तत्र स्थितान यदि भज्यति आत्मभावो पुन कामधातु उपपद्यति यथाभिप्राया ॥

examples.dm: Furthermore, even though they are intensely engaged with the five sensory qualities— Forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures— If they take joy in the Bodhicitta that is free from the vehicles of the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, Know that these heroes are always in meditative equipoise.
examples.gm: Moreover, forms and sounds, and likewise smells and tastes, Touches, and the five qualities of desire, even if they exert themselves in these, If they are free from the vehicles of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening, The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.
examples.sa: किंचापि रूपम् अपि शब्द तथैव गन्धो रस स्पर्श कामगुण पञ्चभि युक्त भोगी । रहप्रत्ययान विगतोऽनन्तबोधिसत्त्वो सततं समाहितु प्रजानयितव्य शूरो ॥

examples.dm: When they have no perception of a body, a mind, or a sentient being, And having turned back from perceptions, they practice the non-dual Dharma— This is what the Benefactor called the perfection of perseverance For those who desire the supreme, undeterred, and peaceful awakening.
examples.gm: Whenever there is no perception of body, mind, and sentient beings, And having completely turned away from perception, one practices the non-dual dharma, For one who desires the supreme, unwaning, peaceful awakening, This was taught by the Benefactor to be the perfection of diligence.
examples.sa: यस्मिन् न कायु न पि चित्त न सत्त्वसंज्ञा संज्ञाविवर्ति स्थितु अद्वयधर्मचारी । अयु वीर्यपारमित उक्त हितंकरेण आकाङ्क्षमाणु शिवम् अच्युतम् अग्रबोधिम् ॥

examples.dm: One who practices patience should also cultivate this thought: "In the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama, there is much suffering. Since I have helplessly experienced harm due to the causes of sensual desire, Why should I not now endure hardship for the sake of enlightenment?"
examples.gm: The one who practices patience should also generate the mind thinking this: "In the hells, animal realms, and the world of Yama, there is much suffering; If one experiences unavoidable harm as a result of sensory pleasures, Why should I not now practice patience for the sake of awakening?"
examples.sa: क्षममाणु एव पुन चित्त उपादितव्यो नरकेषु तिर्ययमलोकि अनेक दुःखा । अनुभूय कामगुणहेतु अकामकारा कस्मा हु अद्य न क्षमेय निदान बोधौ ॥

examples.dm: Having realized that all phenomena are by nature selfless and insubstantial, If they can give away even their own flesh without a discouraged mind, Then at that time, what need is there to mention the giving of external objects? If they were to be stingy, it would be impossible.
examples.gm: Knowing that all dharmas are by nature selfless and insubstantial, If they give away even their own flesh without a shrinking mind, Then what need is there to mention giving away external objects? For them to act with miserliness is impossible.
examples.sa: ज्ञात्वा च धर्मप्रकृतीं वशिका निरात्म्यं आत्मान मांस त्यजमानु अदीनचित्तो । प्रागेव वस्तु तद बाहिर नात्यजेया अस्थानमेत यदि मत्सरि सो करेया ॥

examples.dm: Yet a wise bodhisattva with skillful means Were to rejoice in the substance of those meritorious deeds, And fully dedicate it toward supreme, sublime enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings, By that complete dedication, one will outshine all living beings.
examples.gm: Whatever wise bodhisattva, skilled in means, Rejoices in their bases of meritorious actions, And fully dedicates them to supreme awakening for the sake of beings, By fully dedicating them, they outshine all beings.
examples.sa: यश् चो उपायकुशलो विदु बोधिसत्त्वो तेषां स पुण्यक्रियवस्त्वनुमोदयित्वा । सत्त्वार्थ अग्रवरबोधयि नामयेया अभिभोति सर्वजगती परिणामयुक्तो ॥

examples.dm: Through wisdom, one thoroughly understands the nature of phenomena, And will perfectly transcend the three realms without exception. Having turned the precious wheel, that preeminent leader among men Teaches the Dharma to beings in order to bring suffering to an end.
examples.gm: By wisdom, having fully known the nature of phenomena, One will completely transcend the three realms without exception; The supreme leader of humans, having turned the precious wheel, Teaches the Dharma to beings in order to exhaust suffering.
examples.sa: प्रज्ञाय धर्मप्रकृती परिजानयित्वा त्रैधातुकान्त समतिक्रमते अपायान् । वर्तित्व चक्ररतनं पुरुषर्षभाणां देशेति धर्म जगती दुखसंक्षयाये ॥
